{{Quote|One truth is certain: of all the writers collected in ''The Despotica'', none have come close to beating Peshosloc at the box office.|[[S. V. Skynx/Legends|S. V. Skynx]]|<ref name="Xim Week: The Despotica">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>}}
'''Peshosloc''' was a [[holowright]] who lived between [[15,762 BBY]] and [[15,609 BBY]]. He was the author of ''[[Xim at Vontor]]'' and ninety-odd other [[Holoplay/Legends|holoplays]] written about [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] the Despot, included in the vast literary collaboration known as ''[[The Despotica]]''. He wrote in [[Mid-Galactic Standard]].

Unlike previous ''Despotica'' author [[Lyechusas]], Peshosloc eschewed poetic speech for ostentatious spectacles such as [[Starship/Legends|starship]] battles, exploding [[Moon/Legends|moons]], and solar-system spanning wars. By never writing down to his audience, he was able to make the ''Despotica'' accessible to popular audiences. No other writer collected in ''The Despotica'' was as commercially successful.

Peshosloc's contract stipulated that every [[Hologram/Legends|holo]] derived from his scripts would be subtitled with "based on a true story," leading many to believe what they were watching was historically-accurate, though this was often far from the case. Holos were still being made from Peshosloc's scripts millennia later, and continued to break box office records.
